findings.summary: 3DMLW is a discontinued open-source XML-based markup language for representing interactive 2D and 3D web content. It uses an open-source software suite with its own scripting language and plug-in interface for browser integration. The rendering engine relies on OpenGL and a scene library. A server toolset provides batch conversion and texture atlas generation. Content is viewed via plug-ins for Internet Explorer and NPAPI browsers, though these are no longer available. It supported various 3D model formats and used Lua scripting for animation and events.

mechanisms.title: Rendering pipeline
mechanisms.explanation: The rendering engine uses industry standard OpenGL and consists of a scene library and graphics library providing an optimized pipeline for scene structures. The scene library can be utilized independently for mesh manipulation without rendering.

mechanisms.title: Plug-in interface and scripting
mechanisms.explanation: The plug-in interface mediates input/output between host windows and the application, with native support for common browsers. A Lua scripting facility is provided for animating 3D scenes and handling events, demonstrated by color-fading scripts that modify object attributes.
